newsitem.title: USA: US Southeast power remains weak amid mild weather.
newsitem.headline: US Southeast power remains weak amid mild weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were little-changed Monday, stalled by a lack of weather-driven demand and an ample supply of nuclear power, market sources said.
"It was a repeat of Friday. The market is still very quiet," one market source said.

Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to remain about seven to 14 degrees F above normal through early Wednesday. Near-normal temperatures are forecast for the region Thursday and into the weekend.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak power prices in 16 hour blocks for Tuesday were fairly steady in the $18.50-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range.
Firm, off-peak power for Tuesday at the Ga./Fla. border was still assessed at $13.00-14.00 per MWh.
Florida Power Corp's 750 megawatt (MW) Crystal River 4 coal unit was shut last Thursday due to a transformer fire, but most sources agreed the news had little effect on the market.
FPC said the unit would be shut for a minimum of four weeks for repairs.
In Florida, where temperature highs are forecast to reach the 80s Tuesday, firm, peak power prices on a 16-hour schedule for Tuesday were talked in the $19.00-20.50 range.
Some traders suspected that some limited air-conditioning demand may be preventing the market from softening further.
Firm, peak power prices into Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) for Tuesday were mostly higher in the $14.75-16.00 per MWh range from Friday's trading at $13.75-15.00.
Helping to boost the market was news that TVA's 1,065 MW Browns Ferry 2 nuclear power unit in Alabama was reduced to 29 percent of capacity this morning.
However, TVA's 1,170 MW Watts Bar nuclear power unit, in Spring City, Tenn., resumed full power operations after shutting down a week ago.
Firm, off-peak power prices into TVA were talked in the $12.00-13.00 per MWh range, but no deals were confirmed done.
Separately, Carolina Power and Light's 880 MW Harris nuclear power plant, which tripped off line last Thursday, restarted this weekend and is operating at full power.
Also, Florida Power and Light Co's 666 MW Turkey Point 3 nuclear power unit is back to full power, but its 666 MW unit 4 has been reduced to 40 percent output for cleaning and maintenance.
Georgia Power's 741 MW Hatch 1 nuclear power unit is increasing power and was running at 30 percent output early this morning.
Virginia Power's 781 MW Surry 1 nuclear power unit is nearing full power after shutting down Jan 24 due to a steam pipe leak.
Also, Duke Power's 846 MW Oconee 2 nuclear unit, shut since last September after a steam pipe burst, was in startup early Monday.
Oconee units 1 and 3, shut since October and each generating 846 MW, are expected to restart in February.
((--H McCulloch, New York Power Desk +212-859-1628))
